questions.q: Why is centrifugal casting effective for concrete pipes and poles?
o: It removes the need for curing
It removes the need for cement
Spinning packs concrete against the mold
questions.ref: American Concrete Institute, ACI Concrete Terminology
questions.n: Centrifugal force consolidates the concrete toward the mold wall, producing dense hollow cylindrical products.

questions.q: What is zero-slump concrete?
o: A stiff mix with no measurable slump
questions.ref: American Concrete Institute, ACI Concrete Terminology
questions.n: Zero-slump concrete has very low workability by slump measurement and is commonly consolidated by vibration or specialized equipment.

questions.q: What is segregation in fresh concrete?
o: Separation of the mix into its parts
questions.ref: ACI 304R - Guide for Measuring, Mixing, Transporting, and Placing Concrete
questions.n: Segregation occurs when coarse aggregate, mortar, and paste separate, leading to nonuniform concrete.

questions.q: What is cyclopean concrete?
o: Mass concrete with large stones set in
questions.ref: American Concrete Institute, ACI Concrete Terminology
questions.n: Cyclopean concrete incorporates large stones or rubble within a mass of concrete.

questions.q: What is GFRC?
questions.ref: ACI 544.1R - Report on Fiber Reinforced Concrete
questions.n: GFRC is a cementitious composite reinforced with glass fibers, commonly used in thin architectural panels.

questions.q: Why should excessive segregation be avoided?
questions.ref: ACI 304R - Guide for Measuring, Mixing, Transporting, and Placing Concrete
questions.n: Segregation produces local variations in paste and aggregate content and can contribute to placement defects.

questions.q: Which manufacturing method is commonly used for precast concrete pipes and poles by rotating the mold at high speed?
questions.ref: American Concrete Institute, ACI Concrete Terminology
questions.n: Centrifugal casting uses rotation to compact and distribute concrete in hollow cylindrical products such as pipes and poles.

questions.q: A contractor must repair the underside of a concrete shell without erecting conventional two-sided forms. Which placement method is appropriate?
questions.ref: ACI 506R - Guide to Shotcrete
questions.n: Pneumatic projection makes shotcrete well suited to overhead repairs and irregular surfaces.

questions.q: What generally happens to potential concrete strength as the water-cementitious ratio increases excessively?
questions.ref: Portland Cement Association, Design and Control of Concrete Mixtures
questions.n: Excess mixing water leaves more capillary voids after hydration and drying, generally reducing strength.

questions.q: What is bleeding in fresh concrete?
questions.ref: ACI 304R - Guide for Measuring, Mixing, Transporting, and Placing Concrete
questions.n: Bleeding is the appearance/migration of mixing water to the surface as heavier solid particles settle.

questions.q: Which standard test is used to determine the compressive strength of cylindrical concrete specimens?
questions.ref: ASTM C39/C39M - Standard Test Method for Compressive Strength of Cylindrical Concrete Specimens
questions.n: ASTM C39/C39M is the standard compression test for molded or drilled concrete cylinders.

questions.q: What is the principal purpose of concrete mixture proportioning?
o: The same slump for every mix
questions.ref: ACI 211.1 - Standard Practice for Selecting Proportions for Normal, Heavyweight, and Mass Concrete
questions.n: ACI 211 proportioning balances performance requirements with workable and economical material quantities.

questions.q: A parking surface must allow stormwater to infiltrate through the pavement rather than run off. Which concrete type is appropriate?
questions.ref: American Concrete Institute, ACI Concrete Terminology
questions.n: Pervious concrete is intentionally porous and allows water to pass through its interconnected void structure.

questions.q: What quantity is calculated in a concrete cylinder compression test?
questions.ref: ASTM C39/C39M - Standard Test Method for Compressive Strength of Cylindrical Concrete Specimens
questions.n: Compressive strength is calculated from the maximum axial load carried by the specimen divided by its loaded cross-sectional area.

questions.q: Which mixture parameter has the strongest direct relationship with compressive strength when materials, curing, and air content are otherwise comparable?
questions.ref: ACI 211.1 - Standard Practice for Selecting Proportions for Normal, Heavyweight, and Mass Concrete
questions.n: ACI 211 and PCA guidance relate lower water-cementitious ratio, within practical limits, to higher potential compressive strength.

questions.q: Which document is focused on statistical evaluation of concrete strength-test results?
questions.ref: ACI 214R - Guide to Evaluation of Strength Test Results of Concrete
questions.n: ACI 214R provides guidance for evaluating strength-test data and concrete quality.

questions.q: What is refractory concrete designed to do?
o: Replace structural steel in all cases
questions.ref: American Concrete Institute, ACI Concrete Terminology
questions.n: Refractory concrete is formulated with heat-resistant binders and aggregates for elevated-temperature service.

questions.q: A nonstructural leveling layer is intentionally proportioned with relatively little cement to reduce cost. Which description best fits it?
questions.ref: American Concrete Institute, ACI Concrete Terminology
questions.n: A low-cement, nonstructural leveling or blinding layer is commonly described as lean concrete.

questions.q: A 150 mm-diameter concrete cylinder fails at 530 kN. What is the approximate compressive strength?
questions.ref: ASTM C39/C39M - Standard Test Method for Compressive Strength of Cylindrical Concrete Specimens
questions.n: The circular area is π(150²)/4 = 17,671 mm². 530,000 N / 17,671 mm² ≈ 30.0 N/mm² = 30.0 MPa.

questions.q: What is rich concrete?
o: Concrete with relatively high cement content
questions.ref: American Concrete Institute, ACI Concrete Terminology
questions.n: Rich concrete contains comparatively high cement content.

questions.q: What is a principal advantage of shotcrete placement?
o: It can go on walls and overheads without forms
It can only be cast horizontally
questions.ref: ACI 506R - Guide to Shotcrete
questions.n: High-velocity pneumatic placement allows shotcrete to build up on vertical, irregular, and overhead surfaces.

questions.q: What distinguishes cyclopean concrete from ordinary conventional concrete?
o: Very large stones placed in the mass
questions.ref: American Concrete Institute, ACI Concrete Terminology
questions.n: The defining feature is the inclusion of large stones, much larger than normal coarse aggregate.

questions.q: What is pervious concrete?
o: Concrete with connected voids that drain
Concrete made with fine sand only
questions.ref: American Concrete Institute, ACI Concrete Terminology
questions.n: Pervious concrete is proportioned with little or no fine aggregate to create interconnected voids for drainage.

questions.q: Why are concrete strength-test records important during construction?
o: They show if strength meets the spec
questions.ref: ACI 214R - Guide to Evaluation of Strength Test Results of Concrete
questions.n: Strength-test records are part of quality control and acceptance evaluation for structural concrete.

questions.q: What is lean concrete?
o: Concrete with a low cement content
questions.ref: American Concrete Institute, ACI Concrete Terminology
questions.n: ACI terminology uses 'lean' for concrete with relatively low cement content.

questions.q: What is shotcrete?
questions.ref: ACI 506R - Guide to Shotcrete
questions.n: ACI 506 defines shotcrete as mortar or concrete pneumatically projected at high velocity onto a surface.

questions.q: What is a common purpose of synthetic microfibers in slabs?
questions.ref: ACI 544.1R - Report on Fiber Reinforced Concrete
questions.n: ACI 544 notes that low-volume synthetic microfibers are commonly used to reduce plastic-shrinkage cracking.
